# Egypt E-commerce Sales Analytics

End-to-end analysis of an Egyptian online retailer: data cleaning, BigQuery SQL, customer segmentation, cohort retention, a churn model, and an interactive dashboard.

**Dataset note:** real retail transactions are private, so the data is **synthetic**, generated by `src/generate_data.py` (seeded, reproducible). It has Egyptian seasonality (Ramadan, Eid, White Friday), 6,000 customers, ~14,300 orders (Jan 2025 – Oct 2026), and deliberately messy fields so the cleaning step has real work to do. Findings describe this simulated business, not a real company.

## Key findings

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| How big is the business? | 45.5M EGP net revenue, 12,570 delivered orders, 17.5% gross margin |
| What happened on White Friday 2025? | Revenue spiked to 2.7M EGP but gross profit was about zero: deep discounts erased the margin |
| Which category matters? | Electronics is 67% of revenue at a 10% margin; Beauty (50%) and Fashion (43%) earn far more per sale |
| Do discounts pay off? | Not for Electronics: at 40-50% off it loses about 56% on each sale |
| Who are the best customers? | 973 "Champions" (20% of customers) bring 42% of revenue |
| Best acquisition channel? | Referral: 65% repeat rate and 12.2k EGP per customer vs 41% and 6.5k for paid ads |
| Payment risk? | Cash on delivery cancels 8.5% of orders vs 3.3-3.8% for prepaid methods |
| Does the churn model help? | Barely. ROC-AUC 0.853 (logistic regression) vs 0.833 for a recency-only baseline, so "days since last order" does most of the work |

## What's inside

```
data/          synthetic CSVs (customers, products, orders, order_items)
src/           generate_data.py, analyze.py, verify_sql.py
sql/           BigQuery SQL: clean views, monthly KPIs, RFM, cohorts, channels and discounts
outputs/       result tables and metrics.json
dashboard/     index.html, a static interactive dashboard (Chart.js, works offline)
```

## Method

1. **Clean:** remove duplicate orders (57), standardize 32 city spellings (Arabic and English) to 12 cities, drop the 78 customers with no city (and their 181 orders), label missing payment methods, and drop items whose order was removed.
2. **KPIs:** revenue, margin, AOV, repeat rate, cancellation and return rates on delivered orders.
3. **RFM segmentation:** recency, frequency, monetary quintiles grouped into six named segments.
4. **Cohort retention:** share of each signup month's buyers who order again in months 1-11.
5. **Churn model:** predict whether a customer buys again in the next 3 months from data before a cutoff date, comparing a recency baseline, logistic regression and gradient boosting on a held-out test set.
6. **SQL:** the same logic in BigQuery SQL. `verify_sql.py` runs it in DuckDB on the same CSVs and checks it matches the pandas results (12/12 checks pass).

## Run it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python src/generate_data.py   # optional, data/ is already included
python src/analyze.py         # writes outputs/ and dashboard/data.js
python src/verify_sql.py      # checks SQL against pandas
# open dashboard/index.html in a browser
```

To run the SQL on BigQuery, edit the project ID in `sql/load_to_bigquery.sh`, run it, then run `sql/01_*.sql` through `05_*.sql` in order.

## Limitations

- Synthetic data: patterns such as cancellation by payment method were built into the generator, so the analysis demonstrates method rather than discovering real market facts.
- The churn target ("no purchase in 3 months") is true for 83% of customers, so accuracy-style metrics look flattering; the baseline comparison is the honest benchmark.
- October 2026 has no new signups because the generator stops creating customers on 29 Sep 2026.

## Tools

Python, pandas, scikit-learn, BigQuery SQL, DuckDB, Chart.js.
